alts: el lucro abusivo obtenido con algo
register: Critical economic and journalistic vocabulary for exploiting scarcity or exceptional circumstances to obtain excessive profits.
trap: Profiteering is not ordinary rentabilidad or lucro: it entails taking unfair advantage of a situation, often through excessive prices.
example_tl: La especulación abusiva con medicamentos esenciales permitió a varios intermediarios multiplicar sus márgenes mientras los hospitales afrontaban una escasez evitable.
example_en: Profiteering from essential medicines allowed several intermediaries to multiply their margins while hospitals faced an avoidable shortage.
cloze: {{c1::La especulación abusiva con}} medicamentos esenciales permitió a varios intermediarios multiplicar sus márgenes mientras los hospitales afrontaban una escasez evitable.
note: Materially corrects old_back: lucrativismo is not the idiomatic Spanish term and fails to convey exploitation through excessive profit. Self-review selected a con complement to make the target frame production-ready.

register: Critical technology and political-theory term for treating complex social problems as if technical fixes alone could resolve them.
trap: Solucionismo is critical, unlike neutral orientación a la solución; it questions the reduction of political problems to technical design tasks.
example_tl: El solucionismo tecnológico reduce conflictos políticos complejos a fallos de diseño y desplaza preguntas incómodas sobre poder, intereses y responsabilidad democrática.
example_en: Technological solutionism reduces complex political conflicts to design flaws and displaces uncomfortable questions about power, interests and democratic accountability.
cloze: {{c1::El solucionismo tecnológico}} reduce conflictos políticos complejos a fallos de diseño y desplaza preguntas incómodas sobre poder, intereses y responsabilidad democrática.
note: Old_back has the correct base term but leaves the critical sense underspecified; tecnológico fixes the established concept intended in this topic.

register: Specialist financial-technology vocabulary for representing rights in an asset through digital tokens, particularly on distributed ledgers.
trap: Tokenización also names the segmentation of text in language processing; the complement is essential because the two technical senses are not interchangeable.
example_tl: La tokenización de activos promete ampliar el acceso a la inversión, pero también puede trasladar riesgos financieros a infraestructuras digitales poco supervisadas.
example_en: Asset tokenization promises to broaden access to investment, but it may also transfer financial risks to poorly supervised digital infrastructures.
cloze: {{c1::La tokenización de activos}} promete ampliar el acceso a la inversión, pero también puede trasladar riesgos financieros a infraestructuras digitales poco supervisadas.
note: The legacy term is valid but polysemous. This note deliberately selects the financial-asset sense rather than the language-processing sense.

register: Neutral-formal in media and technology criticism, often used critically for confidence that innovation will produce social progress by itself.
trap: Spanish writes the productive prefix tecno- joined to the base, without the English hyphen: tecnooptimismo, not *tecno-optimismo.
example_tl: El tecnooptimismo dominante presenta cada nueva infraestructura como progreso inevitable y relega sus costes laborales, ambientales y democráticos a simples efectos secundarios.
example_en: Dominant techno-optimism presents every new infrastructure as inevitable progress and relegates its labor, environmental and democratic costs to mere side effects.
cloze: {{c1::El tecnooptimismo}} dominante presenta cada nueva infraestructura como progreso inevitable y relega sus costes laborales, ambientales y democráticos a simples efectos secundarios.
note: Old_back identifies the right term but capitalizes a common noun; the note also makes the closed Spanish spelling explicit.

register: Neutral internet vocabulary, somewhat associated with early online culture but still useful for norms of respectful digital communication.
trap: Spanish adapts English netiquette as netiqueta, with one t and the productive ending -eta; the English spelling is unnecessary.
example_tl: La netiqueta profesional exige corregir información falsa sin humillar al interlocutor, especialmente cuando el debate público ya está marcado por la polarización.
example_en: Professional netiquette requires correcting false information without humiliating the other person, especially when public debate is already marked by polarization.
cloze: {{c1::La netiqueta}} profesional exige corregir información falsa sin humillar al interlocutor, especialmente cuando el debate público ya está marcado por la polarización.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; retention is justified by the adapted Spanish spelling.

register: Formal-critical institutional and legal vocabulary for acting beyond the powers, remit or limits legitimately assigned to an authority.
trap: The English noun is not *sobrealcance; extralimitación normally needs context identifying the authority, power or function whose limits were exceeded.
example_tl: La extralimitación del regulador debilitó una sentencia necesaria, pues el tribunal concluyó que había impuesto obligaciones sin respaldo legal suficiente.
example_en: The regulator's overreach weakened a necessary ruling, since the court concluded that it had imposed obligations without sufficient legal basis.
cloze: {{c1::La extralimitación}} del regulador debilitó una sentencia necesaria, pues el tribunal concluyó que había impuesto obligaciones sin respaldo legal suficiente.
note: Old_back supplies the correct noun but omits its article and institutional frame. Self-review narrowed the example to overreach of legal authority rather than generic excess.

register: Neutral technical and policy usage for software whose source code can be inspected, modified and redistributed under its licence.
trap: Before a Spanish noun, open-source is normally de código abierto, not an English-patterned compound such as *abierto-fuente.
example_tl: La administración eligió una plataforma de código abierto para poder auditar sus componentes, corregir vulnerabilidades y reducir la dependencia de un único proveedor.
example_en: The administration chose an open-source platform so it could audit its components, fix vulnerabilities and reduce dependence on a single provider.
cloze: La administración eligió una plataforma {{c1::de código abierto}} para poder auditar sus componentes, corregir vulnerabilidades y reducir la dependencia de un único proveedor.
note: Materially refines old_back: código abierto names the concept, while the source adjective requires the productive de código abierto construction.

register: Formal and often critical geopolitical metaphor for fragmentation into mutually hostile, isolated or incompatible units.
trap: Balcanización is stronger and more historically loaded than generic fragmentación; Spanish uses c and a written accent on the final ó.
example_tl: La balcanización de internet avanza cuando cada potencia impone estándares incompatibles y obliga a las empresas a duplicar infraestructuras, controles y servicios.
example_en: The balkanization of the internet advances when each power imposes incompatible standards and forces companies to duplicate infrastructures, controls and services.
cloze: {{c1::La balcanización de}} internet avanza cuando cada potencia impone estándares incompatibles y obliga a las empresas a duplicar infraestructuras, controles y servicios.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from capitalization. The exact-duplicate report does not assign this prompt to another topic; the note retains its distinctive rivalry implication.

register: Neutral-formal economics and competition-policy term for a market dominated by exactly two suppliers or platforms.
trap: Duopolio refers specifically to two dominant suppliers; oligopolio is broader and does not preserve that exact numerical distinction.
example_tl: El duopolio publicitario permite a dos plataformas fijar condiciones para los medios, aunque ninguna controle por sí sola todo el mercado.
example_en: The advertising duopoly allows two platforms to set terms for media outlets, although neither controls the entire market on its own.
cloze: {{c1::El duopolio}} publicitario permite a dos plataformas fijar condiciones para los medios, aunque ninguna controle por sí sola todo el mercado.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; retention is justified by the precise contrast with the broader oligopolio.

register: Neutral technical usage; cifrado is concise and widely used, while encriptación is also valid in computing and communications.
trap: Codificación is encoding and does not necessarily conceal information; encryption requires a cryptographic key or equivalent protection mechanism.
example_tl: El cifrado de extremo a extremo protege el contenido de los mensajes, pero no oculta necesariamente quién se comunica ni con qué frecuencia.
example_en: End-to-end encryption protects message content, but it does not necessarily conceal who communicates or how frequently.
cloze: {{c1::El cifrado de extremo a extremo}} protege el contenido de los mensajes, pero no oculta necesariamente quién se comunica ni con qué frecuencia.
note: Old_back is valid rather than erroneous. Self-review selected cifrado as the main term and retained encriptación as a genuine technical alternative.

register: Neutral computing and network-security vocabulary; cortafuegos is the established Spanish equivalent, while firewall remains common among specialists.
trap: Cortafuegos is masculine and has the same written form in singular and plural: el cortafuegos, los cortafuegos.
example_tl: El cortafuegos nacional bloqueó medios extranjeros durante las protestas, pero los ciudadanos siguieron compartiendo copias mediante redes privadas y canales cifrados.
example_en: The national firewall blocked foreign media during the protests, but citizens continued sharing copies through private networks and encrypted channels.
cloze: {{c1::El cortafuegos}} nacional bloqueó medios extranjeros durante las protestas, pero los ciudadanos siguieron compartiendo copias mediante redes privadas y canales cifrados.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate. Retention is justified by the productive non-cognate Spanish term and its invariant plural form.

register: Neutral-formal in statistics, research and algorithmic accountability for a systematic distortion in selection, measurement or outcomes.
trap: Prejuicio is appropriate for a prejudgment or discriminatory attitude, but statistical and algorithmic bias normally requires sesgo.
example_tl: El sesgo de selección distorsionó el estudio porque la muestra excluía a quienes carecían de conexión estable o evitaban las plataformas.
example_en: Selection bias distorted the study because the sample excluded people who lacked a stable connection or avoided the platforms.
cloze: {{c1::El sesgo de selección}} distorsionó el estudio porque la muestra excluía a quienes carecían de conexión estable o evitaban las plataformas.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate but the English prompt is polysemous. The example fixes the statistical sense and separates it from personal prejudice.

register: Neutral technical and policy vocabulary for data describing other data, including communication times, locations, formats or participants.
trap: English metadata often behaves as a mass noun; Spanish normally uses the plural los metadatos, with meta- attached and no hyphen.
example_tl: Los metadatos revelan horarios, ubicaciones y redes de contacto incluso cuando el contenido de las comunicaciones permanece protegido mediante cifrado robusto.
example_en: Metadata reveals times, locations and contact networks even when the content of communications remains protected by strong encryption.
cloze: {{c1::Los metadatos}} revelan horarios, ubicaciones y redes de contacto incluso cuando el contenido de las comunicaciones permanece protegido mediante cifrado robusto.
note: The legacy rendering is lexically correct but omits the article; the note makes Spanish number and prefix spelling explicit.

register: Neutral-critical for innovation presented as breaking with an established model; disruptivo is established but often carries promotional business-jargon overtones.
trap: English disruptive can also mean perturbador or conflictivo; those senses do not describe an innovation that radically alters an industry or model.
example_tl: La empresa presentó como rupturista una función menor, pero su modelo de negocio seguía dependiendo de publicidad invasiva y extracción masiva de datos.
example_en: The company presented a minor feature as disruptive, but its business model still depended on invasive advertising and mass data extraction.
cloze: La empresa presentó como {{c1::rupturista}} una función menor, pero su modelo de negocio seguía dependiendo de publicidad invasiva y extracción masiva de datos.
note: Old_back is valid in business usage. Self-review chose rupturista as the less promotional main term while preserving disruptivo as an alternative for the intended innovation sense.

register: Learned formal adjective for something present across virtually every place or context; omnipresente is more transparent and broadly used.
trap: The Spanish feminine is ubicua, without an accent; Portuguese ubíqua can prompt the incorrect Spanish spelling *ubícua.
example_tl: La vigilancia ubicua convierte gestos cotidianos en señales comerciales y dificulta que los ciudadanos identifiquen cuándo están siendo observados o evaluados.
example_en: Ubiquitous surveillance turns everyday gestures into commercial signals and makes it difficult for citizens to identify when they are being observed or assessed.
cloze: La vigilancia {{c1::ubicua}} convierte gestos cotidianos en señales comerciales y dificulta que los ciudadanos identifiquen cuándo están siendo observados o evaluados.
note: Old_back supplies only an unexplained feminine form and capitalizes it. The production headword is the masculine lemma ubicuo; the example supplies feminine agreement.

register: Neutral-formal in policy and economic analysis; sin regular is compact, while no regulado is equally natural when modifying a noun.
trap: Desregulado often implies that previous controls were removed; it does not always equal something that has never been regulated.
example_tl: Un mercado sin regular permite que los intermediarios trasladen costes a los usuarios antes de que las autoridades comprendan siquiera el modelo.
example_en: An unregulated market allows intermediaries to pass costs on to users before the authorities even understand the model.
cloze: Un mercado {{c1::sin regular}} permite que los intermediarios trasladen costes a los usuarios antes de que las autoridades comprendan siquiera el modelo.
note: Old_back is valid. Retention is justified by the productive sin + infinitive construction and the important distinction from desregulado.

register: Strongly critical in economic and technology commentary for a model or practice that exploits weaker actors for sustained advantage.
trap: Predatory is stronger than merely competitivo: it implies exploitative conduct aimed at extracting value or eliminating weaker rivals.
example_tl: Un modelo depredador ofrece servicios gratuitos hasta eliminar competidores y después impone comisiones que los comercios pequeños apenas pueden asumir.
example_en: A predatory model offers free services until it eliminates competitors and then imposes fees that small businesses can barely afford.
cloze: Un modelo {{c1::depredador}} ofrece servicios gratuitos hasta eliminar competidores y después impone comisiones que los comercios pequeños apenas pueden asumir.
note: The legacy rendering is accurate apart from capitalization. The example fixes the critical business-practice sense rather than literal animal predation. Self-review removed the broader abusivo alternative because it does not necessarily convey systematic predation.

register: Neutral-formal contemporary adjective, often critical when constant network access is linked to exposure, dependency or information overload.
trap: Spanish uses the prefix hiper-, joined directly to the base without the English y or a hyphen: hiperconectado, not *hyper-conectado.
example_tl: Una sociedad hiperconectada recibe información al instante, pero también multiplica la exposición a campañas coordinadas, rumores virales y episodios de acoso.
example_en: A hyperconnected society receives information instantly, but it also multiplies exposure to coordinated campaigns, viral rumors and episodes of harassment.
cloze: Una sociedad {{c1::hiperconectada}} recibe información al instante, pero también multiplica la exposición a campañas coordinadas, rumores virales y episodios de acoso.
note: The legacy rendering is correct apart from capitalization. The example supplies feminine agreement while the production headword remains the masculine lemma.
